Title: Source 2
Subtitle: Matthew Restall, historian, Seven Myths of the Spanish Conquest, 2003
Content: “Other sources produce a similar litany of incidents that add up to overwhelming evidence of the black presence in the Peruvian Conquest. The first four non-natives to see the Inca capital of Cuzco in `text(1533)` included a black man.... During Manco Inca's [Incan ruler] `text(1536)` siege of Cuzco, blacks labored to extinguish the fires on the roof of the royal palace.... A force sent from [the island of] Hispaniola to relieve the defenders included `200` Africans with military experience—a veritable squadron of black conquistadors.”
